There’s more to a Pilgrim
Welcome to a truly special prep school
I really loved my experience at Pilgrims’, both musical, academic and sport. It's a really brilliant place to get a good start in life.
A warm welcome from the Headmaster: Tim Butcher
I attended Pilgrims’ as a boy. I came back as a teacher and I now have the privilege of being the Headmaster. Like I did, boys arrive at a young age still finding their way in the world and experiencing a great many things for the first time. Up to nine years later they leave with confidence and character, knowing they are ready for what is next because they have been stretched through a culture of personalised expectations. This is what we are about. Not producing specialists, honing just a single talent and building everything else around it.
Discover THE Pilgrims’ School
We believe Pilgrims’ offers boys the best start in life at the most crucial time in their development. Our boys work hard and have a lot of fun. Our ‘super curriculum’ offers opportunities unique anywhere at Prep School level and designed to appeal to a boy’s curiosity.
With nearly a century of experience, we’re experts in building boys of good character who enjoy learning, love general knowledge and leave ready to make the world a better place.
We encourage every boy to explore his individual ideas and creativity, something they develop as they move up the school. With numerous music ensembles, multiple choirs, all the sports you can think of and more, up to 50 extra-curricular activities a week, strong drama and LAMDA opportunities, and boarding, we’re a one-stop shop for a comprehensive curriculum, afterschool clubs and wrap-around care combined.
Boarding
Boarding at Pilgrims’ is a truly enriching experience with a great sense of fun and community. We have 100 boarding places, and boys can board from Year 4 onwards.
Creative & Performing Arts
In Pre-Prep, music and creativity are at the heart of daily life, helping boys explore, express themselves, and build confidence through play, song, and imaginative activities.
Admissions
The main points for entry to the school are Reception (4+), Years 3 and 4 (8+/9+). Boys sometimes join other year groups, and at various times in the year, subject to places being available.
Safeguarding and Policies
See all our school policies here.
Location
We are blessed with a truly idyllic location: from London by direct train, with easy access to all the major travel hubs, and surrounded by the stunning countryside of the South Downs National Park.

PERFORMING ARTS
Because all the world’s a stage
PERFORMING ARTS
Drama might look like simply playing a part, but it’s all about human connections. It’s a great way to learn about emotions and feelings. Speaking confidently, working as a team, or communicating with a sense of conviction and compassion – drama is key to developing self-confidence.
Boys have many opportunities to perform, from public speaking and LAMDA competitions to workshops, readings and large-scale productions. Every boy gets involved, on stage or behind the scenes, helping to build confidence and creativity.
Drama lessons often follow themes such as Greek Theatre, Shakespeare or our recent double bill of Agatha Christie where accents, movement and improvisation came into play. Collaborative work encourages boys to express themselves and become articulate performers. We also have several professional theatres nearby with their own productions as well as receiving hit West End tours.
There’s a real focus on a fully rounded education for the boys. There’s not just music, not just sport and not just academic focus – it’s really everything. And that’s important.
LAMDA
The London Academy of Music and Dramatic Art (LAMDA) is one of the country’s top drama schools and an awarding body for Performance and Communication exams.
Taking LAMDA exams in Acting and Verse & Prose develops transferable life skills, encourages friendships, and overall, is a lot of fun.
We have a 100% pass rate and excellent results, but the main benefit is seeing boys grow in self-confidence.
PILGRIMS’ GOT TALENT
An annual event in the school calendar, PGT is a chance for our budding magicians, dancers, comedians, actors, musicians, diabolo masters to showcases the diverse talent we have here.
Boys are judged in true BGT style as they perform to a discerning audience of parents, family, and friends.
PGT became even more popular in 2026 thanks to our very own former Pilgrim, Rafferty Coope.
Rafferty was also a Chorister who made it to the LIVE Final of Britain’s Got Talent, coming 5th with his music and magic performance.
‘I loved my time at Pilgrims’. I was a Chorister and am so grateful to every wonderful teacher who encouraged me whilst reminding me that kindness and being considerate to others was what mattered most’.
DISCOVER MORE
Creative Arts
Creative Arts at Pilgrims’ encourage imagination, expression and confidence, giving boys the opportunity to explore a wide range of artistic and creative disciplines in a vibrant, supportive environment.
English
English is the fundamental to all learning and at Pilgrims’ we provide a thorough grounding in all aspects of literacy.
All boys are encouraged to read and there are plenty of opportunities to explore the world of books.
Sport
Sport at Pilgrims’ plays a key role in developing teamwork, confidence and a love of physical activity, with opportunities for all boys to participate, compete and excel.

MUSIC
Our ISI Inspection (2026) recognised music as a ‘significant strength’
MUSIC & SINGING
Music is everywhere at Pilgrims’. Even if boys don’t play an instrument or sing in one of our choirs, they feel the benefit. We inspire an understanding and appreciation of music which boys find invaluable for the rest of their lives.
From Reception to Year 8, all boys have timetabled class music lessons. We aim to equip each boy with the tools to unlock a deeper understanding of the subject, irrespective of his musical ability.
Neuroscience shows the benefits of music and singing both in terms of inspiring creativity and as a stimulus for brain development.
The Pilgrims’ School Music Showreel – 2025 – YouTube
A unique 'double-choir' school in which almost every boy both sings and learns an instrument - Tatler Schools Guide
LEARNING AN INSTRUMENT
Not surprisingly, there are more instrumental lessons each week than there are boys in the school.
A dedicated team of 28 specialist visiting music teachers means boys can learn any orchestral instrument, in addition to piano, organ, guitar, flute and of course, their voice. Music lessons are arranged so that disruption to lessons is kept to a minimum, ensuring that we preserve the balance between academic subjects, sport, music and free time.
Music practice rooms, including a sound-proofed suite with recording facilities, are mostly located in the music block, but there are pianos, including four grands, dotted all around the school.
Boarders also have timetabled practising slots supervised by the music staff.
MUSICAL ENSEMBLES & PERFORMANCE OPPORTUNITIES
Practising in isolation is one thing, but the stimulus of group music-making is key to a successful musician – it’s also much more fun!
Performing starts in Pre-Prep and, from Year 6 onwards, two-thirds of boys play in ensembles. Boys perform in at least 12 concerts each year, ranging from the formal to the extremely informal. Chamber music is greatly encouraged and music is specially arranged for any ad hoc combinations that may arise when friends decide to pool their resources. The orchestra plays repertoire that one might expect to hear at a senior school.
Ensemble opportunities include, the Jazz Band, the Rock band, Orchestra and Strings, Guitar, Recorder, Woodwind and Baroque Ensembles, as well as Big Band and Orchestra.
The Chamber Choir Tour to Sorrento, that was really memorable. I met lots of lovely people and it really strengthened the bonds within the choir too. That would probably be my favourite memory, but there were so many, it's very hard to choose.
MUSIC EXAMS & SCHOLARSHIPS
Forgive us if we blow our own trumpet…
Graded music exam results for Pilgrims’ boys are consistently high. Most awarded are distinctions or high merits. Many boys attain Grade 5+ each year and pass their Grade 5 theory.
While grades, depth and breadth of repertoire are important, our aim is enjoyment.
We have an enviable record in securing music awards to senior schools, and a significant number of Pilgrims go on to read music at university, many as a choral scholar at either Oxford or Cambridge.
CHOIRS in addition to our CHORISTERS
We know singing is good for us. You’ll hear snatches of song at all times of day.
We have four school choirs including the Chamber Choir who sing for the Christmas Lights switch on every year in Winchester and other high profile events.
The composer, Stephen Barton, a former Pilgrim and Chorister, says
‘Pilgrims’ is a specialist music school in all but title with the finest prep school music department in the country’.
Stephen works regularly with our Choristers on commercial recordings. Our Choristers and Quiristers make up a total of 38 pupils at Pilgrims’.
Winchester is known across the world as a centre of choral excellence and all our Choristers receive what is arguably the best music education in the world.

CREATIVE ARTS
Our setting inspires creativity in all its forms.
ART
We have a wonderful light-filled art studio that’s always buzzing with creativity. Boys are encouraged to explore and experiment with a wide range of media. From watercolours and detailed line drawings to pottery, printmaking and photography, the art curriculum at Pilgrims’ builds confidence and allows every boy to develop his own unique artistic voice. We study a diverse range of artists and makers from all over the world and use their work to inspire and inform our own practice and projects. There are many opportunities for boys to practise art and develop independence and freedom to explore during activity time and commoners. Boys enjoy the art studio as a calm and relaxed space to be creative in their spare time and enjoy extending their own areas of artistic interest e.g. painting, animation, sculpture, illustration and digital art.
A message from Ros Priddle
Head of Art
It’s a dream come true working at Pilgrims’. Our imaginations run wild in the art studio.
It’s a large creative space and I love seeing the boys’ ideas come to life.
For me art is about so much more than teaching drawing, painting or how to make a sculpture. It’s about opening young minds to the world around them and helping our Pilgrims’ express themselves. In terms of development and wellbeing, art provides an essential outlet for boys’ emotions growing up and it’s a privilege to help guide them along the way.
DESIGN & TECHNOLOGY
A Message from Amy Herbert
Head of Design & Technology
Design and technology is the subject where mathematical brainboxes and science whizzkids turn their bright ideas into useful products. James Dyson
IT AND DIGITAL LEARNING
While we keep screen time to a minimum, IT has an important role in education as in the real world.
Our two IT suites have state-of-the-art tech and there’s cross over between what’s taught here and other subjects. Boys enjoy programming robotic models, designing their own games, coding and making films. We also use drones and robots so that the boys can see physical outcomes to their coding. Boys’ learning is enriched with programming in various computer languages, AI and stop-frame animation.
Purple Mash is a platform used by the younger boys to get deeper into their coding journey. Our dancing robot, Polly Pilgrim, offers a different way to code, as well as being good fun to watch.
Further up the school, the boys’ learning is enriched with programming in various computer languages, stop-frame animation, and game creation, as well as making sure they are comfortable with Microsoft Office and editing software. Virtual reality headsets have been very successful in bringing subjects to life through a fully immersive experience. Returning from a visit to the Tutankhamun exhibition, Year 3 put on the VR headsets to find themselves standing in the entrance to an Egyptian tomb. The sense of having been there greatly enhanced the boys’ articles, written for The Daily Hieroglyph after their visit.
Message from Jake Reynolds
Head of Digital Learning
We have a no phones in school policy day to day but there’s no escaping the need for young people to grow up able to understand and use all the tech around us. It means school plays a crucial role in keeping that balance.
You’d be forgiven for thinking my classes are all in, well, the classroom, but far from it. You’re just as likely to see me taking a class in the Quad, coding then racing robots, or filming, before going back inside to edit rushes or create animations.
The world we live in requires a measured response to the technological advances happening day to day, so we take pride in being across it all so we can guide the boy to use digital technology in a positive way.

ENGLISH
THE ENGLISH CURRICULUM
Pilgrims' is an absolutely fantastic school with the most incredible and dedicated teachers. My son is nurtured and encouraged, in all the right amounts. The staff really understand my son and genuinely really care.
ENRICHMENT FOR ENGLISH
Enrichment at Pilgrims’ brings learning to life through theatre trips, author visits and workshops that inspire creativity and insight into the writer’s craft.
Speaking and listening skills are developed through classroom discussion, debate and opportunities to speak in assemblies and services at Winchester Cathedral and Winchester College Chapel, with senior boys also gaining confidence through guiding visitors around the school.
ACCELERATED READER
Accelerated Reader (AR) is a system that helps monitor boys’ independent reading. Pilgrims’ can pick a book at their own level and read it at their own pace. When they have finished, they take a short quiz. AR gives the boys and teachers feedback based to help with what they might want to read next. AR has over 30,000 books on record with quizzes for each, and more are being added every day.
AR keeps a running total of all the words each boy has read. Keeping track of this ‘Word Count’ is something that strongly motivates the boys – the goal is for a boy to become a ‘Word Millionaire’ during an academic year.
BRIGGS LIBRARY
Reading is at the core of the Pilgrims’ way of life, so the library is always open. Boys use it in lessons, breaks, before and after the school or just as somewhere homely to sit quietly and read. Magazines and newspapers are available too with chess sets and comfy sofas.
Our impressive collection of fiction includes the classics alongside the latest releases, while the reference section aims to support the curriculum and to provide material that reflects the boys’ hobbies and interests. We also have the famous P & G Wells book shop just next door where many families enjoy visits from famous children’s authors and workshops.
POETRY RECITAL AND SPEECH COMPETITION
Boys take part in our annual poetry recital, for which they learn a poem and recite it from memory. Older boys also enter our annual speech competition, competing to engage and enthuse audiences, delivering speeches on a topic of their own choice that they have researched and written themselves. The finals of both competitions are judged by an external adjudicator and always well attended by parents.

Geography
Exploring starts in our unique setting
GEOGRAPHY
Our Geography curriculum begins with the boys’ own experiences and surroundings, encouraging them to develop a strong sense of place and belonging. Through exploration of the local environment, outdoor learning and first-hand experiences, boys begin to understand the wider world and their place within it.
Map-making, navigation and orienteering activities help to build spatial awareness, problem-solving skills and confidence in the outdoors, while curiosity-led enquiry encourages boys to ask questions about people, places and the natural world.

SPORT
Sport is part of daily life at Pilgrims’
GAMES & PE
We want all boys to enjoy being active to build skills and confidence. We teach how to play safely and to enjoy healthy competition. Winter sports include football and rugby, while summer focuses on cricket and athletics.
There’s swimming, gymnastics, basketball and badminton. Facilities include extensive pitches at New Piece and Wolvesey, all-weather surfaces and cricket nets, along with outstanding facilities at Winchester College. There’s sailing, tennis, judo and rowing as well.
Our talented sportsmen go on to win senior school sports scholarships. A busy fixtures calendar provides regular competition, balancing performance with participation so as many boys as possible can represent the school.
A message from Myles Greenwood, Director of Sport
We are delighted to be in The Cricketer Magazine’s Top 50 Prep Schools for Cricket. It reflects the dedication of our pupils, and our ambition as a school – an achievement we can all be incredibly proud of.
Even More Opportunities in Sport
Reflecting our close relationship with Winchester College, Pilgrims’ have continued use of the Sports Hall and access to the new climbing wall. We have our outdoor pool but now use the brand-new College pool too.
Our staff are central to our sporting success here at Pilgrims’ so we run games according to the Pilgrims’ Pathway – a comprehensive coaching manual designed for the entire Games Department to provide clear, sport-specific session plans that ensure progressive, age-appropriate coaching and to establish a consistent philosophy for all.
CRICKET
In Years 3 and 4, we begin by playing the pairs version of the game. This allows for plenty of inclusive play as players lose runs, rather than their wicket, for being out. The hard ball is introduced halfway through Year 4. In Year 5, the boys adopt the more familiar 11-a-side format, with the regular laws, and a strong emphasis on the spirit of the game.
Adaptations of the format are adopted as appropriate for the level of any given team, throughout the age groups. Additional coaching sessions in the nets are held after school in the summer term and specialist cricket courses are available in the Easter holidays.
Pilgrims’ boys often play at club, district, or county level.
ATHLETICS
Athletics takes place in PE lessons in the summer and is available as a specialist games option from Year 6. The boys compete against other schools and against each other, working to achieve and better English Schools Athletics Association age-appropriate standards, gain personal bests, and maybe to break school records. Hurdle heights, throwing and running event distances are all age-applicable, and modified equipment may be used.
The Pre-Prep Sports Day is a mixture of competitive races and fun events with lots of family participation, while Athletics Finals, held on Wolvesey, is the culmination of the season for the Prep, a family day of track and field competitions, picnics, and Pimm’s.
FOOTBALL
Played during the Christmas term, the boys follow the FA developmental model with small-sided adaptations, smaller pitches and goals, and no off-sides until Year 7. Holiday courses culminating in a pre-season training week with professional coaches from Southampton Football Club are very popular with the boys. We enter ISFA (Independent Schools Football Association) tournaments at U11 and U13 and nominate candidates for ISFA trials.
RUGBY
Rugby is the main sport during the Lent term. As with soccer, we follow the RFU age grade rules of play. Skills are developed through a greater involvement within the game and a deeper exposure to the skills required. This is particularly reassuring for boys who are new to the sport. Our rugby coaching begins with learning to throw and catch the ball in the Pre-Prep, which develops to tag rugby in Year 3. Contact is introduced in Year 4, solely with the tackle, with technical components adding to the game as it develops to 13-a-side at Year 8.
Staff hold the RFU Rugby Ready qualification as a minimum and the programme is supplemented further with weekly coaching by a specialist. We nominate candidates for the London Irish Developing Player Programme (DPP).
The season culminates with the Rosslyn Park 7s, the largest 7s tournament in the country.
SWIMMING
Weekly swimming begins in Year 1, taught by staff who are highly experienced in developing the skills and confidence of young swimmers. Swimming lessons continue throughout all the year groups.
Water polo is played in our own outdoor pool (known as the Puddle), which the swim squad also use for training sessions. Impromptu swims in the day may also occur in the heat of the summer term when a quick splash in the Puddle helps to focus the mind.
SAILING
The games programme is supplemented by sailing at Spinnaker Sailing Club, near Ringwood and an RYA recognised training centre. The boys travel by minibus and sail a variety of dinghies on the lake.
We sail from the start of the Summer term through to the October half-term break, weather permitting, and it is open to boys from Year 5 upwards, from beginner to top racer!
Boys may be selected to compete at the annual IAPS Regatta at the National Sailing Academy in Portland where they would represent Pilgrims’ in a fleet of Prep School children from all over the UK.
ROWING
Rowing is run in conjunction with Winchester College as a Commoner through the winter terms and as a games option in the summer for boys from Year 7.
FIVES
We are one of the few Prep schools to play Winchester Fives. It’s played in a court similar to a squash court, but with a solid ball and gloves on both hands.
Pilgrims’ boys play the game from the age of 11 as a Commoner activity at the Winchester College courts, while the younger boys begin to learn the game by playing pit-pat – the Pilgrims’ version – against various walls around the school.

SCIENCE
THE CURRICULUM
Boys learn best by doing.
Pilgrims’ scientists are recognised by senior schools for their confidence, practical skills and strong understanding of theory. Our curriculum blends hands-on learning with theory, making science relevant and engaging. By Year 8, boys are confident scientists, often working at GCSE-level practical standard.
In the Lower Prep, science is taught through an investigative approach, helping boys develop skills in the scientific method through prediction, experimentation and evaluation, supported by Forest School in Year 3.
From Year 5 onwards, boys study biology, chemistry and physics as separate subjects, learning in fully equipped laboratories with support from a dedicated lab technician to combine practical skills with theory.
Humanities
Humanities at Pilgrims’ inspires curiosity about the world, developing boys’ understanding of people, places and the past through engaging, hands-on learning.
French
Boys are encouraged to engage with authentic French, developing both confidence and enjoyment of the language.
Mathematics
At Pilgrims’, we encourage boys to become confident, independent thinkers who can question, reason and check their own work.

FRENCH
More than je m’appelle
le programme d’études français
Boys are encouraged to read, listen and engage with authentic French, developing both enjoyment of the language and the ability to hold conversations with native speakers. A strong balance is maintained between grammar and spoken confidence, with boys encouraged to take risks in both writing and speaking. Learning is supported through songs, games, role-play and enrichment activities such as a French film club.
We use a bespoke curriculum, drawing on the Expo scheme, with pupils working ahead of national levels. By Year 8, most grammar is covered, preparing boys for senior school and future study.
At the top of the school, advanced work develops higher-level skills, including translation, discussion and complex grammar through engaging texts. Native speakers are supported with differentiated work and opportunities to further develop their skills, including informal French-speaking events.
There’s a real focus on a fully rounded education for the boys. There’s not just music, not just sport and not just academic focus – it’s really everything. And that’s important.
SPECIALIST LANGUAGE PRACTICE IN YEAR 8
The French curriculum is further enhanced in Year 8 by a weekly intervention from a specialist language teacher. The boys will work individually or in small groups to sharpen and enhance their speaking and grammatical skills. This further reinforces the notion that language is often a communication tool used on a smaller scale. Everyone gets to make progress at their own rate and, like learning any language, often it is the mistakes that we make which help us learn the most effectively.

HUMANITIES
Open minds, wide worlds
GEOGRAPHY
There’s never been a more important time to study Geography. An awareness of the changing climate, social, economic and physical issues is crucial for a better understanding of the world. Debate and discussion are a big part of geography at The Pilgrims’ School. We place a keen emphasis on the ability to empathise with people in different situations and environments around the world.
Geography at Pilgrims’ equips boys with a wide range of skills, from map reading and data analysis to independent research and understanding global cultures and environments.
The curriculum covers key topics such as rivers and coasts, weather and climate, tectonics, population, and sustainability, all designed to encourage connections between subjects and real-world experience.
Learning is highly practical, with regular fieldwork and trips. With the River Itchen, water meadows and the South Downs National Park on the doorstep, boys benefit from rich, hands-on exploration of the world around them.
Achievement in the humanities is high. Pupils are notably articulate and they apply their speaking and listening skills confidently in lessons and discussions. They listen with care to the thoughts and opinions of their peers, happily sharing ideas.
HISTORY
Set among Roman and medieval history in the heart of ancient Wessex, Pilgrims’ offers a rich and inspiring environment for young historians. Boys are encouraged to question, explore and understand the past, building a strong foundation of key events, people and places.
We study Imperial China and world History from Year 3. Learning is brought to life through regular trips and hands-on experiences, including visits to historic sites such as Portchester Castle, Fishbourne Roman Villa and Portsmouth Historic Dockyard, as well as access to the Winchester College Treasury. GENERAL STUDIES
Critical thinking, or ‘General Studies’, is the study of all aspects of the world around us, including politics, ethics, culture, technology.
Boys are taught to question, debate, speculate – to think for themselves.
Critical thinking begins for with a focus on verbal and non-verbal reasoning for younger boys.
n Year 6, we move on to study different human qualities, using, for example, Beowulf and Anne Frank to spark discussions about character traits, motivation, and individual and collective responsibility.
Some of the boys will sit a general paper in their final exam. For these boys in Year 8, critical thinking enables them to construct a discursive argument in response to a question about, for example, the merits of democracy, or the artistic value of modern art.
Through critical thinking, boys are taught to value the power and protocol of written and spoken argument, and to draw their own conclusions.
They may end up seeing the world differently. They certainly become thinkers.

Latin is not a dead language at Pilgrims’
In and out of the classroom
The study of Latin is introduced in Year 6. You might be surprised to know that it’s one of our most popular subjects. Greek is offered as a Commoner after school activity.
Literature and Classical Civilisation
Alongside their linguistic studies, all year groups explore Homer’s The Iliad and Odyssey in translation. Knowledge of these key texts is required at Common Entrance and the boys love listening to scenes from these epic poems. There are also opportunities to learn about:
Roman daily life
Life in the Roman army
The history of Roman Britain
Ancient Greek
Ancient Greek is offered as part of the syllabus in Year 8. We begin by learning the alphabet and progress to reading and translating stories. Working at their own pace, some boys will tackle Ancient Greek scholarship papers, others do the Ancient Greek Common Entrance paper at Level 1 or Level 2. More often than not, boys study Ancient Greek purely to add to their general knowledge.

MATHEMATICS
Inspiring curiosity, logic, creativity, and discovery
THE CURRICULUM
At Pilgrims’, we encourage boys to become confident, independent thinkers who can question, reason and check their own work. We see maths as a way of thinking, aiming to make it engaging, relevant and challenging while equipping boys with the skills to understand and apply it in the real world.
Teaching focuses on building confidence to analyse, make connections and draw conclusions, rather than simply finding the right answer. From the outset, strong numeracy skills are developed, allowing greater focus on deeper thinking as boys progress.
Boys are set to ensure the right level of challenge, working across numbers, measures, shapes, graphs and statistics, with algebra becoming increasingly important as they move through the school.

NATIONAL COMPETITIONS
Boys in Years 5 and 6 can take part in the Primary Maths Challenge and the Junior Maths Challenge, organised by the Mathematical Association.
Both are national competitions that allow the boys to pit their wits against other pupils across the country and to win awards for their mathematical prowess.
